“State legislatures should have the right to regulate any stricter laws than that,” [...] “The ultimate decision on where to allow data centers to be built should be controlled at the local level though ordinances and zoning restrictions.”

But the concern of having a data center, electric use drive up the cost of the rest of the consumers is legitimate. We passed a bill with, I think it was 417 to 3 out of the House in September that requires states to require data centers to pick up all of the infrastructure upgrade costs that it takes to tie to the grid and to have make sure they have policies that don't negatively impact the water supply, water infrastructure.
There's parts of Indiana that want them. There's parts of Indiana that don't. And that is perfectly fine in the way it should be.
